lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the Talinum-style superior ovary and longitudinally valved capsule as the close split from Portulaca.

project_scope.selection_mode: Talinum-centered project module with taxonomy cleanup
project_scope.note: Current Kew accepts Talinum aurantiacum and treats Phemeranthus aurantiacus as its synonym; both source rows remain visible for provenance.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Look for a somewhat succulent herb, commonly with 2 sepals, 5 petals and a superior one-celled ovary containing many ovules. The fruit is a many-seeded capsule opening by longitudinal valves rather than a circumscissile lid.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Annual or perennial somewhat succulent herbs or subshrubs; leaves alternate to subopposite or rosulate; stipules absent.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers commonly in terminal or axillary cymes/racemes/panicles; sepals 2; petals usually 5; stamens 5 to many; ovary superior and one-locular.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A dry many-seeded capsule, commonly opening by 3 longitudinal valves.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: If it looks purslane-like but the capsule splits into valves instead of popping a lid, think Talinaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: succulent habit → 2 sepals/5 petals → superior ovary → 3-valved capsule → taxonomy note
visual_lesson.intro: Talinaceae is the close relative that makes the Portulacaceae comparison useful: similar flower plan, different fruit opening.

steps.title: 1 · Compare the flower with Portulaca
steps.look_for: Usually two sepals, five petals and many stamens on a succulent or tuberous herb.
steps.why_it_matters: The shared flower plan reveals the close Caryophyllales relationship.

steps.title: 2 · Follow it to a valved capsule
steps.look_for: A many-seeded capsule opening into longitudinal valves, commonly three.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the practical split from Portulaca's circumscissile capsule.

steps.title: 3 · Learn the current-name wrinkle
steps.look_for: Phemeranthus aurantiacus in older/source material maps to accepted Talinum aurantiacum in the current project taxonomy.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents duplicate learning cards for the same accepted taxon.

comparisons.title: Talinaceae vs Portulacaceae
comparisons.rule: Talinum: superior ovary + longitudinally valved capsule. Portulaca: ovary often partly inferior + circumscissile lid-opening capsule.

comparisons.title: Talinaceae vs Caryophyllaceae
comparisons.rule: Talinaceae commonly has succulent leaves and only 2 sepals; Caryophyllaceae usually has opposite leaves and 4–5 sepals with a different capsule architecture.

visual_lesson.caveat: Older literature may place Talinum and Phemeranthus differently. This learner follows the current accepted project/Kew treatment for the taxa in the pool.

genera.fast_cue: somewhat succulent/tuberous herb + 2 sepals + superior ovary + 3-valved capsule
source-name lane; P. aurantiacus folds to Talinum aurantiacum in current Kew treatment
